# nodejs-errors.dev

> Authoritative reference for Node.js error messages: exact causes, step-by-step fixes, and code examples for the most common runtime errors encountered by Node.js and npm developers.

## Home

- [nodejs-errors.dev](https://nodejs-errors.dev/): Index of all Node.js error pages.

## Error Pages

- [MODULE_NOT_FOUND](https://nodejs-errors.dev/MODULE_NOT_FOUND/): Thrown as `Error: Cannot find module '...'` when `require()` cannot locate an npm package or local file. Covers nine causes including missing install, typos, wrong path, working directory, devDependencies in production, case sensitivity, corrupted install, TypeScript path aliases, and Docker.
- [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED](https://nodejs-errors.dev/ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED/): Thrown when importing a subpath (e.g. `some-package/lib/utils`) not listed in the package's `"exports"` field in `package.json`. Covers root cause, five fix strategies, affected Node.js versions, and a debugging checklist.
- [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM](https://nodejs-errors.dev/ERR_REQUIRE_ESM/): Thrown when `require()` is used to load a pure ES module. Covers how to use dynamic `import()`, how to convert to ESM, and a table of popular packages that went ESM-only with their last CJS versions.
- [ENOENT](https://nodejs-errors.dev/ENOENT/): Thrown as `Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory` when a file system operation targets a path that does not exist. Covers path typos, working directory issues, missing directories, async race conditions, and case sensitivity.
- [EADDRINUSE](https://nodejs-errors.dev/EADDRINUSE/): Thrown as `Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::PORT` when a server tries to bind to a port already in use. Covers how to find and kill the conflicting process on macOS, Linux, and Windows, and how to implement graceful shutdown.
- [ECONNRESET](https://nodejs-errors.dev/ECONNRESET/): Thrown as `Error: read ECONNRESET` or `Error: socket hang up` when the remote server sends a TCP RST packet, forcibly closing the connection. Covers stale keep-alive sockets, load balancer idle timeouts, retry logic with exponential backoff, socket timeouts, and `keepAliveTimeout` tuning.
- [ECONNREFUSED](https://nodejs-errors.dev/ECONNREFUSED/): Thrown as `Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:PORT` when Node.js tries to connect to a host and port where nothing is listening. The OS immediately rejects the connection. Covers six causes (service not running, wrong port, wrong host/IP, service crashed, firewall, Docker networking), and five fixes: verify service is running with `lsof`/`netstat`, correct host/port config, Docker Compose service names, retry with exponential backoff, and health-check patterns.
- [TypeError-Cannot-read-properties-of-undefined](https://nodejs-errors.dev/TypeError-Cannot-read-properties-of-undefined/): Thrown as `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'x')` when a property is accessed on an undefined value. Covers six causes and fixes including optional chaining, null checks, async data races, and API response validation.
- [ETIMEDOUT](https://nodejs-errors.dev/ETIMEDOUT/): Thrown as `Error: connect ETIMEDOUT`, `Error: read ETIMEDOUT`, or `FetchError: network timeout` when a TCP connect or read operation exceeds the timeout window with no response from the remote host. Covers six causes (firewall packet drop, overloaded server, DNS failure, short default timeout, slow upload, DNS resolution timeout), and five fixes: `AbortSignal.timeout()`, `req.setTimeout()`, exponential backoff retry, `dns.lookup()` diagnostics, and distinguishing connect vs read timeouts via `err.syscall`.
- [ENOTFOUND](https://nodejs-errors.dev/ENOTFOUND/): Thrown as `Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND hostname` when DNS resolution fails and the hostname cannot be translated to an IP address. Also covers `EAI_AGAIN` (temporary DNS failure). Covers seven causes including hostname typos, missing connectivity, wrong environment variables, Docker container DNS issues, VPN/corporate DNS, and how to verify, retry, and handle DNS errors gracefully in production.
- [EMFILE](https://nodejs-errors.dev/EMFILE/): Thrown as `Error: EMFILE: too many open files` when the Node.js process exceeds the OS per-process file descriptor limit. Covers five causes (bulk file I/O without closing, file watchers in webpack/jest/chokidar, concurrent HTTP sockets, fd leaks, low ulimit), and six fixes: raising ulimit on macOS and Linux, batching with p-limit, using graceful-fs for automatic retries, closing file handles with try/finally, limiting watcher scope, and detecting fd leaks with lsof.
- [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE](https://nodejs-errors.dev/ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE/): Thrown as `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "path" argument must be of type string. Received undefined` when a Node.js built-in receives an argument of the wrong JavaScript type. Almost always `undefined` instead of a string for `path`, `data`, or `chunk` arguments. Covers seven causes (undefined env var, missing return value, forgotten `await`, wrong type to stream.write/response.end, destructuring from null, unset environment variable, broken package.json main field) and six fixes: assert before passing, validate env vars at startup, nullish coalescing defaults, fixing missing await, typeof guard before built-in calls, and clearing npm cache for npm ERR! ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE.
- [ReferenceError-document-is-not-defined](https://nodejs-errors.dev/ReferenceError-document-is-not-defined/): Thrown as `ReferenceError: document is not defined` (also `window is not defined`, `navigator is not defined`, `localStorage is not defined`, `location is not defined`) when browser-only globals are accessed in a Node.js environment that has no DOM. Covers six causes (direct DOM access in shared isomorphic code, importing browser-only npm libraries, SSR rendering components that access document outside useEffect, Jest/Vitest using the default node test environment, browser globals accessed at module load time, third-party analytics scripts used in SSR) and six fixes: typeof guard (`if (typeof document !== 'undefined')`), Next.js dynamic import with ssr: false, moving browser code into useEffect (React) or onMounted (Vue), configuring testEnvironment: 'jsdom' in Jest/Vitest, creating separate browser and server entry points with the package.json browser field, and globalThis polyfill patterns for test environments.
- [EPIPE](https://nodejs-errors.dev/EPIPE/): Thrown as `Error: write EPIPE` when a write is attempted on a stream, socket, or pipe whose reading end has already been closed. Most common when piping Node.js output to `head`, `grep`, or `less` (the consumer exits early closing its stdin), writing to an HTTP response after the client disconnected, streaming to a child process stdin after the child exited, or writing to a TCP socket whose remote end closed. Covers six causes, six fixes: handling EPIPE on `process.stdout` with `process.exit(0)`, guarding HTTP response writes with `res.writableEnded`, listening for the `'close'` event to stop streaming, using `stream.pipeline()` instead of manual `pipe()`, attaching `'error'` handlers to all writable streams, and destroying streams on unexpected EPIPE. Also covers when EPIPE is expected (piping to head/grep) versus a real bug (database socket, child process stdin).
- [UnhandledPromiseRejection](https://nodejs-errors.dev/UnhandledPromiseRejection/): Thrown as `UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning` (Node.js < 15) or as a fatal `UnhandledPromiseRejection` crash with exit code 1 (Node.js 15+) when a rejected Promise has no `.catch()` handler or `try/catch` around an `await`. Covers the critical Node.js 15 behavioral change (warning → fatal crash), six common causes (missing await/catch, promise chain without .catch(), async event listener, async setTimeout/setInterval callback, unreturned middleware promise, fire-and-forget without error handling), and eight fixes: try/catch in async functions, .catch() on promise chains, wrapping async event listeners, wrapping async timer callbacks, using `process.on('unhandledRejection')` as last resort only, enabling the `@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises` lint rule, replacing `forEach(async)` with `Promise.all(arr.map(async))`, and wrapping Express async route handlers with an asyncHandler helper or upgrading to Express 5.
- [SyntaxError-Cannot-use-import-statement](https://nodejs-errors.dev/SyntaxError-Cannot-use-import-statement/): Thrown as `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module` (also `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement in a script` and `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'`) when ESM `import`/`export` syntax is used in a file Node.js parses as CommonJS. Covers six causes (missing `"type": "module"` in package.json, mixing ESM and CJS, ts-node without ESM config, Jest without ESM transform, copying ESM code into a CJS project, ESM-only dependency) and six fixes: adding `"type": "module"` to package.json, renaming to `.mjs`, converting to `require()`, enabling ts-node ESM mode with `--esm` flag or `tsconfig.json`, configuring Jest with `transform: {}` and `--experimental-vm-modules`, and Babel CJS transform. Also covers the relationship with ERR_REQUIRE_ESM, file extension comparison table (.js/.mjs/.cjs), and `__dirname`/`__filename` unavailability in ESM scope.
- [JavaScript-heap-out-of-memory](https://nodejs-errors.dev/JavaScript-heap-out-of-memory/): Fatal V8 crash printed as `FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory` (also `FATAL ERROR: CALL_AND_RETRY_LAST Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory`). Not a JavaScript Error object — no `err.code`, cannot be caught with try/catch or uncaughtException. Process exits with code 134 (SIGABRT) or is killed by the OS OOM killer (exit code 137). Covers six causes (loading large JSON/CSV entirely into memory, memory leaks from retained event listeners or closures, unbounded arrays/Maps/caches, build tools like webpack and next build, deep recursion, default V8 heap too small at 1.5 GB on 64-bit) and six fixes: increasing heap with `--max-old-space-size=4096` (command line, NODE_OPTIONS, Next.js/webpack build scripts), streaming large files with `fs.createReadStream` + `readline` or `csv-parse` streaming API, processing data in fixed-size batches, fixing memory leaks with `emitter.off()`, WeakMap caches, and clearing intervals, diagnosing leaks with `--inspect` + Chrome DevTools heap snapshots and `process.memoryUsage()` logging, and offloading to `worker_threads` or `child_process.fork()` with separate V8 heap per worker.
